chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

There is no believer who lends to another believer, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that its reward is counted for him according to the reckoning of charity until his wealth returns to him.

key_terms.أَجْرُهَا: its reward; the spiritual recompense for the act
key_terms.أَقْرَضَ: gave a loan; extended wealth to another with the expectation of return
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: charity; voluntary giving for which divine reward is granted
key_terms.مَالُهُ: his wealth; the property that was lent out and later returned
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer; the one described as giving or receiving the loan within the community of faith
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: the Face of Allah; meaning His pleasure and acceptance
key_terms.يَلْتَمِسُ: seeking; aiming sincerely for a higher purpose

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving a loan to a believer for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that giving a loan to a fellow believer sincerely for the sake of Allah carries the reward of charity. The lender continues to receive that reward until the borrowed wealth is returned, showing the great spiritual merit of helping others financially without selfish motive.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "There is no believer who lends to another believer seeking the pleasure of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, except that it is counted for him as the reward of charity until his money is returned to him."
